name: Naukuchiatal
extract:
Naukuchiatal or "lake of nine corners" is a small hill station and lake near Nainital Town in Nainital district of Kumaon, Uttarakhand, India. Its chairman is Devendra Singh Chanotiya.
The lake is 175 feet deep and is situated at 1,220 metres (4,000 ft) above sea level. It is the deepest lake in the Nainital region. The length of the lake is 983 metres (3,225 ft), its breadth is 693 metres (2,274 ft) and it has a depth of 40.3 metres (132 ft). Naukuchiatal is also known for the 'escape festival' which happens once every year (in the month of May).


Location
The lake is situated 4 km from Bhimtal and 26 km from Nainital. The nearest railway station is in Kathgodam.


Mythology
It is believed that the lake was created after hard worship (Sanskrit "tap") of Brahmaji and a small temple dedicated to Brahmaji exists near the KMVN guesthouse. According to locals anyone performing a parikarma of the lake will be blessed by Brahmaji.


Climate
The temperatures in summer range from 11 C to 26 C and in winter from -2 C to 14 C.


Notable locations


Hanuman Temple
Hanuman Temple is situated on the main road to Naukuchiatal. It has a 52 foot tall statue of Lord Hanuman. The Temple has an artificial cave design on the lines of the famous Vaishno Devi Shrine. The temple premise is very clean, which helps connect with the spiritual world immediately upon arrival. The temple also houses Vaishno Devi temple, Shani Mandir, and Ram Darbar temples and a reflection and place to sit back and rest for the visitors.


Mukteshwar
Mukteshwar is a temple situated at a distance of 38 km from Naukuchiatal set at an elevation of 2,285 m above sea level.  Mukteshwar is named after a 350-year-old temple called Mukteshwer Dham whose presiding deity is great Lord Shiva. The top of the mountain on which Mukteshwar Dham is stood offers views of the Himalayan range.  Mukteshwar was developed by the British as a research and education institute by setting up Indian Veterinary Research Institute (IVRI) in 1893.


Sat Tal ('Seven Lakes')
Sat Tal is a cluster of mysteriously interconnected seven freshwater lakes (Purna Tal, Ram Tal, Sita tal, Laxman Tal, Nal Damyanti Tal, Sukh Tal and Garud Tal) situated 19 km away from Naukuchia Tal. Sat Tal is set at an altitude of 1,370 m above sea level. The group of lakes is set amidst dense forests of oak and pine trees. These lakes are a notable home for
migratory birds as they stay for some time here during their migration. 


Nainital
The busiest hill station in the Kumaon region of Uttarakhand state.  It is situated at a distance of 33 km from Naukuchia Tal at an elevation of 1,938 m above sea level. Nainital is named after an eye shaped lake set amidst the mountains with thick alpine trees.


Almora
Almora is known for its panoramic view of the Himalayas, cultural heritage, wildlife, handicrafts and cuisine. It is located at a height of 5,400 ft above sea level and is spread across a 5 km ridge atop Kashaya Hill. It is surrounded by Pithorgarh to the east, Garhwal to the west, Bageshwar to the north and Nainital to the south. The landscape of Almora attracts hundreds of tourists each year. It is situated 72 km from Naukuchiatal.


Ranikhet
Ranikhet is situated 7 3 km from Naukuchiatal at an altitude of 1,869 m above sea level.  Ranikhet is a hill station in Almora District of Uttarakhand state and is maintained by Ranikhet Cantonment Board. Ranikhet is also the home for the Kumaon and Naga regiments of the Indian Army.


Bhim Tal
Bhim Tal is situated at a distance of 5 km from Naukuchia Tal at an altitude of 1,375 m above sea level.  The main attraction in Bhimtal is the Bhimtal Lake which has a small island at its centre. Bhimtal is an ancient place named after the legendary Bhima of Mahabharata when Bhima visited during the exile period of Pandavas. 


Haldwani
Haldwani is situated in the Nainital district of Kumaon region of Uttarakhand state at an average elevation of 425 m above sea level. The hills of the Kumaon region commence from Haldwani and the temperature decreases as climbers ascend. Since the beginning Haldwani has been a trading hub of Kumaon.

wikivoyageExtract:
Naukuchiatal is one of the most beautiful hill stations in Kumaon in Uttarakhand. It is known for its breathtaking smoky mountains, 175-foot-deep Nine Corners Lake, paragliding and other adventure activities.


Understand


Get in
The lake is 4 km from Bhimtal and 26 km from Nainital. 


By rail
The nearest railway station is Kathgodam.


By plane
The nearest airport in Pantnagar (PGH IATA) just 56 km driving distance from Naukuchiatal.


Get around

Naukuchiatal is nicely connected with the different towns, with buses frequently running.


See

 Bijroli Village, Naukuchiatal Road (1 km distance away from Hanuman Mandir, above Green Valley Hotel). A small village (Gaon) near Pandeygaon on Naukuchiatal Road, surrounded by lush-green smoky mountains and home to hundreds of bird species, this village is about 800 m away from Bhaktidham Ashram and 1.2 km from Naukuchiatal Lake. (updated Feb 2019)

1 Jungaliagaon, Near Bijroli (5 km driving distance from Naukuchiatal Lake). Jungaliagaon is a small village 7500 ft above sea level, popular amongst nature and paragliding lovers and home to more than 200 bird species. (updated Feb 2019)
 Sattal Lake (Sat Tal) (near Bhimtal and Naukuchiatal hill stations). An interconnected group of seven freshwater lakes in the Lower Himalayan Range. (updated Feb 2019)
 Hanuman Mandir Bhaktidham (Hanuman Garhi), Naukuchiatal Rd (near Kamaltaal). 52-foot-high statue of the monkey god Hanuman. It has a Vaishno Devi gufa (cave) as well. A separate Durga temple allows elderly folks to have darshan without going through the gufa. (updated Feb 2019)


Do
There are opportunities of angling and bird watching in the valley. Other activities include parasailing, paragliding, fishing, rowing, paddling and yachting.

Hot air balloon ride
Mountain/quad biking  One can do enjoy quad biking ride near Naukuchiatal or Lotus (Kamal) Lake.
Shikara boating in one of the deepest lakes (185 feet) of Nainital district.
Paragliding (There are 12 paragliding points located on the road going to Jungaliagoan)
Kayaking
Zip River Crossing
Rope Cycling
Fishing
Zorbing
Trekking


Buy
 Mini Shopping Mart, Naukuchiatal Road (4 km away from Naukuchiatal). Apart from the main Bhimtal market, there are multiple local shops on Naukuchiatal Road itself from where one can buy all daily essential products easily. (updated Feb 2019)


Eat
 Do Baati Restaurant, Naukuchiatal Rd, ☏ +91 72480 26677. Valley view restaurant popular amongst tourists visiting Naukuchiatal or Bhaktidham temple. (updated Feb 2019)
 Balaji Restaurant (opposite Hanuman Mandir Bhakti Dham), ☏ +91 97193 96447.  (updated Feb 2019)
 Aipan Restaurant, Naukuchiatal Rd, Siloti Pant, ☏ +91 72528 56687. within walking distance from Naukuchiatal & Lotus Lake. (updated Feb 2019)
 Cafe by the Lake, Naukuchiatal Road, ☏ +91 73107 93352. 11AM to 8PM. Calming garden cafe by the lake with a menu based around the cuisine of Greece. (updated Feb 2019)


Drink
Whisky, beer and wine shops can be found in Bhimtal market, just 5 km driving distance away.


Sleep
 The Royal Homestay, Bijroli Village, ☏ +91 97564 79092, info@theroyalhomestay.com. Check-in: noon, check-out: 11AM. The interior of this homestay can accommodate more than 6 guests and it has 3 designer bedrooms (attached bath), dining table for 6, and fully-equipped kitchen with balcony facing the mountains. (updated Feb 2019)
 Club Mahindra Resort, Bohra Gaon, Nainital, ☏ +91 80064 02770. Set on over a hectare of lush grounds overlooking Naukuchiatal lake. (updated Feb 2019)
 The Bungalows, Village Bohragoan, ☏ +91 95550 88000.  (updated Feb 2019)
